title.value: NeuroDiversity: The Birth of an Idea

date.reason: Legacy citation/Singer bibliography identify a 2016 Kindle edition, while the cited Wellcome locator describes a 2017 print edition; v0.2 requires a full YYYY-MM-DD date.

neurodiversity-claim-1.finding: Singer's work reproduces her 1998 sociology honours thesis, includes participant-observer research on the InLv internet community of autistic people, and situates the emerging movement in late-1990s disability-rights and autistic-community activity.
neurodiversity-claim-1.population_or_context: Late-1990s autistic self-advocacy and disability-rights context, including Singer's participant observation of the InLv internet community and autobiographical/family material.
neurodiversity-claim-1.methodology: Sociological honours thesis combining participant observation on InLv, autobiographical self-exploration, historical discussion, and post-modern, social-constructionist, feminist and disability-rights analysis; later book editions reproduce the thesis with a new introduction.

limitations.statement: Singer is a participant in the history being reconstructed, and this source alone cannot determine exclusive or complete origin attribution.
limitations.why_it_matters: The claim concerns distributed historical credit, so participant testimony and retrospective framing require comparison with dated independent records and other early participants.
limitations.reopening_or_reduction_condition: Compare dated primary records and contextualised accounts from multiple early autistic-community participants.

neurodiversity-claim-2.finding: Singer's work treats the emerging neurodiversity paradigm within disability-rights discourse, maps an emerging category of disability, critiques social-constructionist fundamentalism, and argues for balancing medical accounts with sociological or adaptive models of neurological difference.
neurodiversity-claim-2.population_or_context: Autistic people and related neurological minorities considered within late-1990s disability-rights, autistic self-advocacy, sociological and medical-model debates.
neurodiversity-claim-2.methodology: Qualitative sociological and participant-observer analysis combining disability-rights theory, social constructionism, feminism, autobiographical material and observation of an autistic online community.

limitations.statement: Accessible descriptions support coexistence of disability and social or political framing but do not directly establish every claim element about support needs and clinical care.
limitations.why_it_matters: A broad compatibility claim should not be upgraded into person-specific clinical or support guidance without direct evidence.
limitations.reopening_or_reduction_condition: Review the relevant thesis or book passages and additional primary evidence that addresses support needs and clinical care explicitly.

neurodiversity-perspective-paradigm.held_by_scope: Neurodiversity advocates and scholars using disability-rights, sociological and inclusion-oriented framings; not a claim that all neurodivergent people, clinicians, researchers or advocates hold one position.
neurodiversity-perspective-paradigm.reasoning: Singer's work situates neurological variation within disability-rights, social-constructionist and feminist analysis, combines autobiographical and autistic-community observation, and argues for balancing medical accounts with sociological or adaptive understandings rather than treating diagnosis as the whole meaning of difference.
neurodiversity-perspective-paradigm.scope: A social and political framing of neurological variation, disability, rights, environment, inclusion and movement-building; excludes individual diagnosis, person-specific support prescriptions and any claim that all neurological differences are beneficial.

title.value: The neurodiversity concept was developed collectively: An overdue correction on the origins of neurodiversity theory

authorship.value: Monique Botha; Robert Chapman; Morénike Giwa Onaiwu; Steven K Kapp; Abs Stannard Ashley; Nick Walker

citation_correction.value: Botha, Monique; Chapman, Robert; Giwa Onaiwu, Morénike; Kapp, Steven K; Stannard Ashley, Abs; Walker, Nick. The neurodiversity concept was developed collectively: An overdue correction on the origins of neurodiversity theory. Autism (2024). doi:10.1177/13623613241237871.
citation_correction.reason: Legacy DOI is 10.1080/09687599.2024.2327837; the cited Portsmouth publication record identifies 10.1177/13623613241237871. Preserve legacy v0.1 text unchanged.

neurodiversity-claim-1.finding: Botha and colleagues identify Singer's 1998 thesis in the InLv autistic-community context, Harvey Blume's 1997 and 1998 published uses, and a reported 1996 InLv discussion, and conclude that neurodiversity's concept and theorising have multiple, collective origins rather than a single originator.
neurodiversity-claim-1.population_or_context: Historical development of neurodiversity in autistic online-community discussion and published writing from the mid-to-late 1990s, analysed by an international group of autistic scholars of autism and neurodiversity.
neurodiversity-claim-1.methodology: Peer-reviewed scholarly letter synthesising recent archival findings, dated published texts and attribution history to correct a single-origin account of neurodiversity.

limitations.statement: The letter synthesises selected archival and published evidence and may not capture every early contributor or inaccessible community record.
limitations.why_it_matters: The claim concerns historical credit, where incomplete archives or decontextualised mailing-list material could distort attribution.
limitations.reopening_or_reduction_condition: Extend contextualised archival comparison and obtain accounts from multiple early participants where ethically and practically possible.

neurodiversity-perspective-collective.held_by_scope: Botha, Chapman, Giwa Onaiwu, Kapp, Stannard Ashley and Walker as an international group of autistic scholars writing on the historical origins of neurodiversity; not a statement representing all autistic people or all neurodiversity scholarship.
neurodiversity-perspective-collective.reasoning: The authors compare dated archival and published evidence from autistic online-community discussion, Singer's 1998 thesis, Blume's 1997 and 1998 writing, and a reported 1996 InLv post, and conclude that the concept and theorising of neurodiversity have multiple, collective origins.
neurodiversity-perspective-collective.scope: Historical attribution of the origins and early theorising of neurodiversity; excludes ownership of later meanings, a complete history of every contributor, and representation of all contemporary neurodiversity positions.

decision_candidates.question: Which edition should the future v0.2 Singer Evidence object represent: the legacy-cited 2016 Kindle edition or the Wellcome-located 2017 print edition?
decision_candidates.recommended_action: Do not choose or combine editions until the intended source identity and a schema-valid full date are explicitly resolved.

decision_candidates.question: Should the future non-authoritative v0.2 Botha Evidence citation use the verified DOI 10.1177/13623613241237871 while preserving the legacy v0.1 DOI unchanged?
decision_candidates.recommended_action: Accept the verified citation correction for the future v0.2 Evidence candidate only; preserve the v0.1 source text exactly.
